trust_decision.summary: Whether a network request is from an allowed client is decided in internal/middleware/ip_whitelist.go from gin's c.ClientIP(); that value is produced outside the check, by the engine's trusted-proxy set fixed once at router/routers.go:47, and it is also the key of the login-ban bucket in api/user/auth.go:51, so one bundled proxy makes every client look like 127.0.0.1 and both the allowlist and the ban bucket collapse.

landing_point.why: The only line in the whitelist middleware that lets a request through without consulting IPWhiteList: clientIP == "" (unparseable peer) and clientIP == "127.0.0.1"/"::1" both short-circuit, which is exactly what a bundled reverse proxy produces for every user.

fix_sites.entry_point: every /api/* HTTP route and the embedded static UI via middleware.IPWhiteList()
process bootstrap: gin engine trusted-proxy configuration used by c.ClientIP() for all routes
engine trusted-proxy defaults merged from NGINX_UI_OFFICIAL_DOCKER / NGINX_UI_DISABLE_BUNDLED_NGINX at startup
shipped sample app.ini used by new installations

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Re-adding 127.0.0.1 and ::1 to the trusted proxies reads as re-introducing the very bypass the report describes, and it only fires for the official Docker image, so a solver can argue that default belongs to the deployment and not to the fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Direct loopback access must keep working without being listed in IPWhiteList: it is documented behaviour, it is how an admin on the host or over an SSH tunnel gets in, and the fix keeps it while adding a test that a forwarding header from an untrusted peer is still ignored. Deleting the 127.0.0.1/::1 exception, or trusting every peer's headers instead, breaks one side or the other.

O6_input_shapes: X-Forwarded-For comma chain with a client-supplied spoofed prefix (rightmost untrusted hop wins)
forwarded headers sent by a peer that is not a configured trusted proxy (must be ignored)
IPv4 peer, IPv6 loopback peer, and CIDR trust entries such as 10.0.0.0/8 and 2001:db8::/32
empty or unparseable peer address (must fail closed with 403 instead of passing)
empty trusted-proxy list (nil, no header is trusted)
settings payload shape: JSON array of strings carrying the __NGINX_UI_REDACTED__ placeholder

O7_producer.where: settings/settings.go:33 registers AuthSettings for NGINX_UI_AUTH_* / app.ini (struct at settings/auth.go:3-7); the loaded value is turned into the engine's trusted-proxy set at startup in the new router/client_ip.go (fix.diff:1669-1682)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Routes registered on the engine before initEmbedRoute installs the global IPWhiteList chain - /healthz always, and /pages/maintenance in an unembed build - never pass the allowlist gate at all.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A liveness probe and a maintenance page have to stay reachable from an unconfigured load balancer and they expose no application data.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the router bootstrap, 0 packages from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: WebSocket upgrade origin check accepts Forwarded / X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Proto from any peer and uses them as the request's own origin, with no trusted-proxy gate.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the cross-site-WebSocket origin check, a neighbouring feature; the advisory is about client IPs and this setting lists origins, not proxies.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the landing point, different file and different sink

O8b_injection_room.sibling: passkey login recomputes the client address itself (X-Forwarded-For split) instead of calling c.ClientIP()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The passkey path already duplicates the password path's ban bookkeeping (compare api/user/auth.go:51 with api/user/passkey.go:239), so a maintainer adding a third login path would plausibly read the header directly.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second topology default for the demo container (resources/demo/nginx-ui.conf) added next to the bundled-nginx loopback default
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: There are already two shipped front-proxy configs; the next deployment topology that proxies from a fixed address gets the same helper extended.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the forwarded host/proto used for the origin check is gated on the same TrustedProxies list
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix's own rule ('only trusted proxies may supply forwarded headers') applies verbatim to this code, so a follow-up hardening would copy the ClientIP gate here.

O9_family: improper authorization from trust in an unvalidated client identity (CWE-346 origin validation error): the bundled reverse proxy makes every client share the 127.0.0.1 identity, so the IP allowlist short-circuits for everyone and all logins feed one ban bucket

O10_build.toolchain: go build / go test (cgo needed for mattn/go-sqlite3 via gorm.io/driver/sqlite); bun for app/ tests
services: none for the affected tests (httptest, in-memory SQLite)
nginx only for the bundled-proxy deployment scenario
O10_build.project_tests: internal/middleware/middleware_test.go, mcp/router_test.go:28-46 (sets IPWhiteList and exercises /mcp), api/user/security_test.go, api/user/passkey_security_test.go; the fix adds internal/middleware/ip_whitelist_test.go, router/client_ip_test.go and internal/user/login_ban_test.go, none of which exist at the pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete the 127.0.0.1/::1 and empty-IP short-circuits in IPWhiteList() and stop there: every proxied user is then 403'd, while the ban bucket still keys on 127.0.0.1.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix commit is a bundled release commit: app/src session-expiry, HTTP error normalisation, nginx dashboard, release notes, PRODUCT.md and index-CustomMMDB changes are unrelated to this advisory and were not screened.
resources/demo/nginx-ui.conf:28-31 serves /var/log/nginx/demo-boot.log from the demo front proxy; outside this advisory, not pursued.
